draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Hampi! By 1500 this was probably the world's second-largest city after Beijing, the grand capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, and today its ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat in my notes for Hampi, so wander through Hampi Bazaar and see what's cooking.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Virupaksha Temple is just a 4 min walk, and Sunset Point is about 6 minutes away. Hemakuta Hill with its temples is right by the bazaar too.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Climb Matanga Hill late in the day, people say it has the most beautiful sunsets in Hampi.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Rock climbers from all over have been coming to Hampi for more than 30 years just to scale its boulders.

legends.title: Hanuman's birthplace
legends.body: Across the river, the Hanuman Temple on Anjenaya Hill is believed to be where Hanuman was born. Getting there means climbing 572 steps.

legends.title: A Ramayana past
legends.body: Local legend takes the history of Anegundi, across the river, all the way back to the Ramayana. Hampi itself may have been the Kishkindha of that age.

tips.title: Start early on a bicycle.
tips.body: Cover the southern temples in the cool morning, spend midday in the museum, and save the Vithala Temple for late afternoon.

tips.title: Plan around the combined ticket.
tips.body: One ticket covers the Vithala Temple, the Lotus Mahal area and the Archaeological Museum, and it's only valid for one day.

story.title: Pampa's holy place
story.body: Hampi shows up in the Ramayana, the Puranas and Ashokan inscriptions as Pampa Devi Tirtha Kshetra. The Virupaksha Temple here was first built in the 7th century.

story.title: City of Victory
story.body: After Delhi Sultanate armies plundered the Deccan, the Sangama brothers founded Vijayanagara from the ruins. Hampi was its capital from 1336.

story.title: Richest city in India
story.body: Persian and Portuguese travellers wrote about a wealthy city full of temples, farms and markets by the Tungabhadra. The Achyutaraya temple, finished in 1534, was the last one built before the fall.

story.title: The fall
story.body: After the Battle of Talikota, a coalition of sultanates conquered and destroyed the capital. Hampi was abandoned.

story.title: Ruins and pilgrims
story.body: Since the 19th century the ruins have drawn archaeologists and historians, and they're now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Virupaksha is still a living temple and the main centre of pilgrimage here.
